public_rationale: The most cited measure of long-task ability is METR's time horizon. In December 2025, METR said Claude Opus 4.5 had a 50% horizon of about 4 hours 49 minutes, the 'nearly five hours' Shumer cites, but an 80% horizon of only 27 minutes, in line with earlier models. METR's tasks are mainly software, ML, and cybersecurity work, not all human tasks. So as of the post, no measured system came close to doing five-hour tasks reliably, let alone without error. Even by May 2026 the best reported 80% horizon was about three hours. The side remark that hallucinations are 'so common' was not measured separately.
limitations: The METR figure is taken from a faithful reproduction of METR's thread, not METR's own site.
The hallucination-frequency clause is vague and was not assessed with data.
No benchmark measures 'every' five-hour human task.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: No current AI system comes close to reliably doing every five-hour task humans can do without error, and hallucinations and boneheaded errors remain common in everyday use.

statement.excerpt: No AI system can reliably do every five-hour long task humans can do without error, or even close, but you wouldn’t know that reading Shumer’s blog, which largely ignores all the hallucination and boneheaded errors that are so common in every day experience.

our_interpretation: The core testable part: as of the post, no AI system came anywhere near high-reliability performance on five-hour human tasks.
The best public yardstick is METR's 80%-time horizon, a stricter measure than the 50% one. 'Reliably ... without error' implies an even higher bar.
'Or even close' is read as: the best high-reliability horizons were well below five hours, for example under about half of it.
The clause about hallucinations being 'so common' is a vague framing and is treated as secondary.
criteria.support_condition: Public measurements from the period show frontier systems' high-reliability (80%) time horizons well below five hours, even on METR's coding-focused tasks.
criteria.contradiction_condition: A public measurement from the period shows an AI system completing five-hour human tasks at high reliability (80% or more) across a broad range of domains.

evidence.excerpt: Despite its high 50%-time horizon, Opus 4.5's 80%-time horizon is only 27 minutes, similar to past models and below GPT-5.1-Codex-Max's 32 mins.
evidence.explanation: The model Shumer cites for 'nearly five hours' succeeds 80% of the time only on tasks of about 27 minutes. That is far from reliable five-hour performance.
